title: Activity

workstates.title: Work contexts
workstates.hint: Explicit snapshots, kept for 30 days. Search scans up to 50 records per page: continue even when a page has no matches.
workstates.captureHint: Enter only what you want to keep. The server removes sensitive text and URLs and applies your private words; this is not a guarantee of removing all personal data. Quick capture uses the desktop app, not browser tab access.
workstates.urlsHint: One HTTP(S) URL per line, up to 20. Query strings, fragments and unsafe addresses are removed by the server.
workstates.invalidCapture: Check the fields: text up to 160 characters; up to 20 URLs, each up to 2048 characters.
workstates.saved: Context saved. Active search and time filters still apply.
workstates.captured: Desktop capture accepted. If queued offline, it will appear after sync. Active filters still apply.
workstates.notCaptured: No context was captured. Capture may be canceled, unavailable or blocked by privacy settings.
workstates.timezone: Dates and time filters use this device's time zone: {{timezone}}.
workstates.invalidRange: Enter valid dates with From no later than To, and a search of at most 160 characters.
workstates.error: The operation failed. Check your connection and try again.
workstates.authError: Access denied or session expired. Sign in again to continue.
workstates.empty: No contexts on this page for these filters.
workstates.emptyPage: No matches in this batch. More records are available: continue searching on the next page.
workstates.restoreHint: Only the listed targets may be opened. Branches and notes are references: no commands run and no automatic Git checkout occurs. Opening local projects requires desktop confirmation.
workstates.browserRestore: Native resume is unavailable here. Open individual web links yourself; local paths are text only.
workstates.emptyPlan: No safe actions remain in this context.
workstates.resumeResult: Opened: {{opened}}; failed: {{failed}}. References are not executed.

digital.title: Digital activity on this computer
digital.hint: These are local desktop permissions, not browser-extension settings. Missing measurements are not zero; no biometric or fatigue assessment is made.
digital.telemetryHint: Aggregate activity only, not typed text or key logs. Input counts are supported only in VisualStudio. Terminal metrics require the explicit terminal wrapper; arbitrary terminals and commands are not monitored.
digital.smartBreakHint: Optional suggestions after observed work and supported transitions. Requires desktop telemetry and its supported sources; it does not detect fatigue and is not a guaranteed timer.
digital.desktopOnly: Requires a compatible desktop app. This control does not enable browser collection.
digital.unavailable: Not available now: check desktop tracking, permissions and telemetry settings. An existing consent can still be turned off.
digital.error: Could not confirm the setting. Refresh to read its actual state before trying again.

empty: Nothing was recorded in this period.
mostlyOther: Most of the time is in “Other”: the programs have no category yet.

setup.title: No tracker yet
setup.hint: Time is recorded by the desktop app of the dashboard: open the dashboard in it and switch tracking on in the Setup tab. It then starts with the computer, sits in the tray and sends what it records by itself.
setup.devicesMoved: The trackers of the devices and the time of devices without one are in

timeline.title: The day, window by window
timeline.empty: Nothing was recorded on this day.

tracker.title: Trackers
tracker.browser: Time is recorded by the desktop app of the dashboard. Open the dashboard in it to switch tracking on for this computer.
tracker.unsupported: The tracker can watch windows only on Windows for now.
tracker.off: Tracking is off on this computer. When it is on, the app records which program and window is in front and sends it to your server.
tracker.refused: The desktop app did not take this computer. Restart the app and try again.
tracker.removed: This computer was removed from the devices, so its tracking stopped. Switch it on again to register it anew.
tracker.merge: Move its records to another device
tracker.confirmMerge: Everything “{{from}}” recorded goes to “{{into}}”, then “{{from}}” is removed. Continue?

idle.title: When you are away
idle.hint: No keyboard or mouse input for this long means you have left; the time is not counted. A full-screen video in a player or a browser counts as activity anyway, for up to 3 hours; a game left without input does not.
idle.label: Away after

rules.title: Projects
rules.hint: Time goes to a project when the window title or the site's address contains its name. Add other words a project is recognized by: a folder, a repository, a site, localhost:4200.
rules.noProjects: There are no projects yet: create one in the settings.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.hint: Once a day the AI looks at the windows and sites that turn up in work on projects (localhost with the running app, for example) and offers them here. Only what you accept becomes a rule.
suggestions.near: {{time}} next to work on the project in 2 weeks

apps.title: Programs
apps.hint: The category of each program, and whether it is recorded at all. Switching a program off deletes what was recorded for it.
apps.empty: Programs appear here as the tracker sees them.
apps.confirmExclude: Stop recording “{{name}}” and delete what was recorded for it?

focus.browser: Focus sessions run in the desktop app: open the dashboard there to start one. The statistics are here in any case.
focus.enableTracker: Switch tracking on for this computer in the Setup tab: focus sessions are sent with it.
focus.empty: No focus sessions in this period.

music.title: Focus and music
music.hint: What played during the sessions, from the listening history.
music.result: {{completed}}% finished, {{distracted}}% of the time lost to distractions

computers.noData: Has not reported its state yet
computers.empty: No computers yet: switch tracking on in the Setup tab.
computers.hint: The desktop app reports every 5 minutes. A notification comes when a disk has less than a tenth free or Windows marks it as failing, when Windows has been slowing the processor down for a quarter of an hour to cool it, and when the computer has not been restarted for two weeks. The last 30 days are kept. Real processor temperatures need administrator rights and a sensor driver, so the temperature here is the board sensor Windows gives.
computers.throttling: the processor is slowed down to cool it
computers.outagesWeek: Outages in the last week: {{count}}, {{minutes}} min in all

wellbeing.title: Breaks, limits and focus
wellbeing.hint: The desktop app reminds to take a break, and a notification comes when a daily limit is reached (all devices together, once a day).
wellbeing.gamesPerTaskHint: The limit of games grows with the tasks you finished today.
wellbeing.noBonus: Nothing: the limit is the same every day

disk.title: Free up space
disk.thinking: The AI is looking at what was found…

safety.safe: Safe: it is rebuilt by itself
safety.check: Most likely not needed — have a look first
safety.risky: Your own data — only you know

disk.trash: Move to the Recycle Bin ({{gb}} GB)
disk.confirm: Move these to the Recycle Bin?
disk.emptyBin: The space is freed when the Recycle Bin is emptied.

reasons.protected: protected (the system, programs or a virtual disk) — left as it is
reasons.unknown: not in the last scan — scan again
reasons.failed: Windows did not move it (in use, or too big for the Recycle Bin)

disk.confirmEmpty: Empty the Recycle Bin of {{mount}}? The files in it are deleted for good.
disk.emptied: The Recycle Bin is empty: the space is free.

npm-cache.confirm: Clear the npm cache? Packages are downloaded again when needed.

yarn-cache.confirm: Clear the Yarn cache? Packages are downloaded again when needed.

pip-cache.confirm: Clear the pip cache? Packages are downloaded again when needed.

nuget-cache.confirm: Clear the NuGet caches? Packages are restored on the next build.

docker-prune.confirm: Remove all Docker images not used by a container, stopped containers, unused networks and the build cache? Volumes stay. Docker Desktop must be running. Images are downloaded again when needed.

disk.stale: This scan is old: the disk has likely changed since. Scan it again with the button in the disk's row.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.hint: Windows whose title contains one of these words are recorded without the title: only the program. Private windows of browsers (Incognito, InPrivate, private browsing) are always recorded this way.

otherComputers.title: Time from other devices
otherComputers.hint: The app sees only the computers it runs on. The time below comes from other services and is added to the Overview; switch off what should not be counted.
otherComputers.tracked: Not added, the app already counts their time: {{names}}

explain.wakatime: Time in an IDE from WakaTime: the least you worked there
explain.steam: Steam games beyond those the app has seen itself
explain.extension: Sites from the extension while neither the app nor WakaTime saw anything: the browser on a laptop, for example

otherComputers.included: Including {{time}} the app has not seen: an IDE and the browser on computers without it, and games from Steam. Time that overlaps is counted once.

telemetry.observations: Measured buckets only; gaps are unknown. Boundary totals are proportional estimates; devices can overlap. Not a health or productivity assessment.

desktop.buildWaitHoursDay: Desktop: {{value}} h of measured build wait
desktop.inputPerMinute: Desktop: input events per measured minute
desktop.inputPerMinuteDay: Desktop: {{value}} input events per measured minute
desktop.terminalErrorPercentDay: Desktop: {{value}}% failed commands among paired measurements
desktop.backspacePercentDay: Desktop: {{value}}% backspaces among measured input events

browser.buildWaitHoursDay: Browser: {{value}} h of measured build wait
browser.inputPerMinute: Browser: input events per measured minute
browser.inputPerMinuteDay: Browser: {{value}} input events per measured minute
browser.terminalErrorPercentDay: Browser: {{value}}% failed commands among paired measurements
browser.backspacePercentDay: Browser: {{value}}% backspaces among measured input events

life.dayFocus: {{hours}} h of screen time, mostly {{app}} · {{focus}} focus sessions

automations.place: Place (its name in Activity → Places; empty — any)

links.phoneNight: On the phone late at night (23–4)

phone.rest: Rest from the phone at night
phone.media: Music and video on the phone

browser.title: Browser
browser.hint: What the browser extension does: it counts the time on each site (only the site, never the address of a page; never private windows and sites with a private word), closes distracting sites during a focus session of the desktop app, and closes a site whose daily time is spent. "Open anyway" lets it in for 5 minutes.
browser.track: Count the time on each site
browser.distractingHint: A subdomain counts too: youtube.com closes m.youtube.com.
browser.limitsHint: Every browser with the extension together; once the time is spent, the site is closed until tomorrow.

diagnostics.title: Why it is on or off

collection.unsupported: This computer cannot collect digital telemetry: it works on Windows only.
collection.unregistered: This computer is not tracked yet. Turn on tracking of this computer in Setup.
collection.no-server: The desktop app has no server address. Choose the server in the app's tray menu.
collection.consent-required: Telemetry is off. Turn on "Allow digital telemetry" above if you want it.
collection.stopped: The tracker of this computer is stopped. Turn tracking on in Setup or in the tray.
collection.paused: Tracking is paused. Resume it from the tray when you want.
collection.locked: The computer is locked: nothing is collected until it is unlocked.
collection.suspended: The computer was asleep: collection starts again by itself.
collection.idle: You are away from the computer: nothing is collected until you are back.
collection.private-window: A private window is in front: it is never collected.
collection.excluded-app: The program in front is in the list of programs never recorded.
collection.waiting-window: Waiting for the next look at the window in front — a few seconds.
collection.collecting: Collecting: the numbers go to the server once a minute.

diagnostics.breaksNeedTelemetry: Break suggestions need the digital telemetry turned on.

delivery.failed: failed — the next minute tries again

diagnostics.sessionOnly: This is what the app saw since it started; nothing of it is kept. "Accepted" means the server took the request.
diagnostics.windows: App switches and focus: any program, once a minute, without names or titles.
diagnostics.input: Typing rhythm: only in the editor of Visual Studio (devenv). Not in VS Code, Rider, terminals or browsers.
diagnostics.terminal: Build and test times: only for commands run through Invoke-PdCommand.
diagnostics.browser: The browser extension does not send this telemetry; its own settings are in the extension.
diagnostics.browserOnly: Open this page in the desktop app to see why the telemetry is on or off.
diagnostics.oldDesktop: The desktop app is older than this page: restart it to get the update and see the reasons.
diagnostics.error: Could not read the state of the desktop app. Refresh to try again.

notifications.none: No notifications from the phone yet. Switch the collection on in the Android app: Settings → Devices.

places.none: The phone told nothing about this day. Allow the location in the Android app: Settings → Devices → The phone as a sensor.
places.few: Too few points to tell the places of this day.

import.title: The Google Maps timeline
import.hint: Import your past places from Google: Takeout (Location History — Records.json or Semantic Location History) or Maps on the phone → Settings → Location → Export Timeline data (Timeline.json). The file is read here; only the points go to your server.
import.done: Imported {{saved}} new points of {{read}}; places named by Google: {{names}}.
import.failed: Nothing to import: this is not a Google Maps timeline file.

places.googleFailed: Google did not answer: check the Places key in Settings → Integrations
places.name: Name it
places.namePrompt: The name of the place (Home, Work…)
places.frequentHint: Name a place, and its stays take the name

period.label: Period of the map
period.hint: Where the time went from {{from}} to {{to}}: the darker, the more hours. Circles are your named places.

phone.nightHint: At night — in apps of the phone from 23:00 to 4:00; the night counts to the evening it began on.

signals.title: The phone, an average day
signals.hint: Over the days the phone told each; settings of what it collects — Settings → Devices

google.subtitle: Optional: without them OpenStreetMap names the places and draws the map
google.placesKey: Google Places key (stays on the server)
google.mapsKey: Google Maps key (for the map, seen by the browser)
google.placesSaved: Google Places is connected: a place has "Look up on Google"
google.mapsSaved: Google Maps is connected: Activity → Places can switch the map
google.invalid: Google did not take the key

guide.1: Open Google Cloud Console and make a project (or pick one); a billing account is needed, the free monthly credit covers personal use.
guide.2: APIs & Services → Library: enable "Places API (New)" and "Maps JavaScript API".
guide.3: Credentials → Create credentials → API key, twice: one for Places, one for Maps.
guide.4: Restrict the Maps key: Application restrictions → Websites → your dashboard's address and https://localhost/* (the Android app). Restrict the Places key to the Places API.
guide.5: Paste each key here and save: the Places key is checked against Google.
